pr_body:
With this commit, terminal will be able to copy text to the system
clipboard by using OSC 52 MANIPULATE SELECTION DAATA.

We chose not to implement the clipboard querying functionality offered
by OSC 52, as sending the clipboard text to an application without the
user's knowledge or consent is an immense security hole.

We do not currently support the clipboard specifier Pc to specify which
clipboard buffer should be filled

# Base64 encoded `foo`
$ echo -en "\e]52;;Zm9v\a"

# Multiple lines
# Base64 encoded `foo\r\nbar`
$ echo -en "\e]52;;Zm9vDQpiYXI=\a"

Closes #2946.

Being new to this project here are the steps I followed in case anyone wants to verify/reproduce my manual test:
- Clone `https://github.com/uzxmx/terminal`
- Clone submodules: `git submodule update --init --recursive`
- Built with powershell `Import-Module .\tools\OpenConsole.psm1` followed by `Set-MsBuildDevEnvironment` then `Invoke-OpenConsoleBuild`
- Opened Visual Studio 2019, set build mode for CascadiaPackage project to `Release` and `x64`
- Started the project then in the ensuing terminal used the `echo -en "\e]52;foo\a"` examples outlined in the PR to confirm expected text is placed on the standard windows clipboard.

> So, we read text to copy from stdin, then check if it’s length exceeds the maximum length of 74994 bytes. If true, we crop it, and finally convert data to base64 and wrap in OSC 52 escape sequence: \033]53;c;${data_in_base64}\a

- iTerm2 has quite a long list of [quite useful OSC codes](https://www.iterm2.com/documentation-escape-codes.html) and while non-standard, lot's of interesting ideas there. Including notifications and arbitrarily large clipboard updates.

@hh  Agree with you. The reason I made this PR is that I really need to rely on this feature when I ssh into a vagrant box.

Considering you mentioned tmux and vim, I also want to share some of my experiences. Actually without OSC 52 support, I've already been able to copy to and paste from windows system clipboard when using tmux and neovim. 

My environment is:  Windows Terminal + Ubunt WSL + Nvim (only in WSL enough) + Tmux.

The core principle is to pipe text to `clip.exe` (provided by Windows system) and get clipboard contents by a get-from-clipboard executable (Windows system hasn't provided) or some command from powershell. It works the same way as pbcopy/pbpaste in OSX system.

Unlike vim, Nvim provides clipboard providers, so we can easily add a custom provider. Here are the [reference](https://github.com/uzxmx/dotfiles/blob/master/vim/plugin/wsl.vim) for nvim and [reference](https://github.com/uzxmx/dotfiles/blob/1f2350899000812384472a955a9d049f7a56f47f/tmux.conf#L92-L96) for tmux configuration in my dotfiles repo. This [article](https://uzxmx.github.io/wsl-tricks.html#access-windows-clipboard-in-nvim-on-wsl) gives more details on that and it also summarizes serveral WSL tricks. 

But without  OSC 52 support, it's impossible to do that on a remote machine.

This is incorrect:
~~~~
echo -en "\e]52;foo\a"
~~~~
1) OSC 52 takes two arguments, the first of which is the clipboards to set (empty default).

2) The text must be Base64-encoded.

Take a look at: https://invisible-island.net/xterm/ctlseqs/ctlseqs.html

~~~~
Ps = 5 2  ⇒  Manipulate Selection Data.  These controls may
          be disabled using the allowWindowOps resource.  The parameter
          Pt is parsed as
               Pc ; Pd
          The first, Pc, may contain zero or more characters from the
          set c , p , q , s , 0 , 1 , 2 , 3 , 4 , 5 , 6 , and 7 .  It is
          used to construct a list of selection parameters for clip-
          board, primary, secondary, select, or cut buffers 0 through 7
          respectively, in the order given.  If the parameter is empty,
          xterm uses s 0 , to specify the configurable primary/clipboard
          selection and cut buffer 0.

          The second parameter, Pd, gives the selection data.  Normally
          this is a string encoded in base64 (RFC-4648).  The data
          becomes the new selection, which is then available for pasting
          by other applications.

@nicm
 
Thanks for pointing out that information. Really helpful. I referenced tmux's OSC 52 implementation, and finished adding base64 mechanism to make it conform to the standard.

@zadjii-msft

Changes have been made. Please have a look. Currently, the first parameter `Pc` is ignored. So it always uses the system clipboard. 

When the parameter is neither a valid base64 string nor `?`, the standard says `the selection is cleared`. So would you suggest we clear the content of the system clipboard?

Another question is should we implement below in this PR? Actually I tried to experiment, but have no success. I didn't find the event hook when a newline for shell prompt e.g. `>` appears, or something that's called ready to accept user input, or some function to feed some string after a new prompt. If this feature is required, could you give me some guidance?

```
If the second parameter is a ? , xterm replies to the host
with the selection data encoded using the same protocol.  It
uses the first selection found by asking successively for each
item from the list of selection parameters.
```

So, the question about supporting clipboard _query_: I don't think we should. It's generally regarded as a security boundary issue if an application, especially a _remote_ one, can silently request a read from your clipboard. We'd need to build up some infrastructure to make sure that that operation is permitted before we add support for it! 

It's very good that this pull request only adds the clipboard overwriting half :smile:

issue_context.title: Support xterm VT sequence (OSC 52) for setting the clipboard
issue_context.body:
Mintty and xterm support options to allow setting the clipboard by VT sequences, a feature used by tmux to sync its internal clipboard with the system clipboard.  I also wrote the patch for `st` to add support for setting Xorg's PRIMARY clipboard from VT as well as supporting OSC 52 clipboard setting in tmux if it is emitted from something like vim or a remote nested tmux instance (see [patch](https://github.com/tmux/tmux/pull/734/commits/ff59b153a07eaec578cba0b2abf8912aed5e8bc7)). 

The current code in `st` is under 

```
strhandle(void)
{
[...]
case 52
```

in [st.c](https://git.suckless.org/st/file/st.c.html), where it is implemented in a few lines (and the low-level logic is clearer than in my tmux snippet). Notice that the first argument is ignored (since it is only used to read back the system clipboard, which is insecure for reasons spelled out below).

Implementation:
The documentation for this control sequence in xterm is available on [invisible-island](https://invisible-island.net/xterm/ctlseqs/ctlseqs.html) (see OSC Ps for Ps = 52). The documentation isn't amazing, but essentially the data is emitted as base64 and is decoded back to UTF-8 by base64dec.   I don't know how you would implement this into the Windows clipboard, which iirc still uses USC2/UTF-16, but base64dec does give you back a UTF-8 string, and reencoding that to a string compatible with the Windows clipboard is probably something that I think is just handled nowadays by a standard Windows API.

Potential security implications:
I would leave this setting as optional and on a profile-by-profile basis (gated behind an option 'allowClipboardSharing', in case a nasty script emits uses this to try to write data to the clipboard (which at least in the past had been the source of an exploit in an older version of Windows).  Note: I would _not_ add support for the _read_ portion of the control sequence (my tmux patch for example simply ignores this case), since this would allow unauthorized reading of the system clipboard.  

Example Use Case:
https://sunaku.github.io/tmux-yank-osc52.html

Note that X11 forwarding is not really a desirable option just for clipboard sharing in Windows, given that the Windows clipboard is not an X clipboard, and X11 forwarding theoretically has the same security implications (in fact worse implications).
comments:
Let me also ephasize the security aspects of this feature.

> in case a nasty script emits

It doesn't necessarily mean a malicious script. It could be a poorly coded application combined with an attacker-supplied input, such as [OpenSSH's SCP client](https://sintonen.fi/advisories/scp-client-multiple-vulnerabilities.txt) (bullet points 3 & 4) as discovered recently, or another example mentioned in [VTE's issue tracker](https://bugzilla.gnome.org/show_bug.cgi?id=795774).

> I would leave this setting as optional [...] I would not add support for the read portion

Sounds to me the most reasonable approach, if this feature is implemented at all. Another idea from the VTE bug is to present a popup dialog to confirm setting the clipboard (although it's sure annoying after some time).

Whenever [this spec](https://github.com/microsoft/terminal/pull/2840) is implemented, and clipboard-setting from within the terminal is implemented, I think even I (a non-programmer) could write this patch.  My only concern is with mixing levels, since I'm not sure if this spec is for the terminal application or for plain conhost, since I think VT processing is done at the level of conhost, rather than at the level of the Terminal, and if the option will be controlled by the profiles.json, I don't know how to turn on a setting at the level of conhost.

Sure - here's an outline that's largely copy pasted from https://github.com/microsoft/terminal/issues/3004#issuecomment-590984729:

I think is involved here is roughly:
* [ ] Change the `OutputStateMachineEngine` to be able to parse these sequences and _pass them through_ to the connected terminal, when the console is operating as a conpty. (this might already work).
* [ ] When the state machine isn't in conpty mode, it'll need to call methods on `ITerminalDispatch`. These should be left unimplemented for conhost. I believe that means no-op'ing them in `adaptDispatch`, or probably just returning false.
* [ ] For the Windows Terminal, these `ITerminalDispatch` methods (implemented in `TerminalDispatch`) should call (new) methods on `ITerminalApi`, implemented in `Terminal`. 
* [ ] These `Terminal` methods should probably trigger some sort of callback, that `TermControl` can listen for.
* [ ] `TermControl`'s callback should be able to raise the copy event like it already does, but now with the data provided by the VT sequence, instead of from the selection.

And I think it might _just work_.
